subject: Mutual onboarding plan: Dedicated GPU pool for AtlasAI — regional staging & SLA runbook
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@atlasai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-ops@atlasai.com
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding for AtlasAI

Neha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. AtlasAI is ready to move forward with Dedicated capacity for our inference workloads. To keep momentum, we'd like to lock down a short mutual action plan around regional selection, autoscaling/bursting parameters, and an SLA runbook that covers canary traffic and fallback.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Confirm preferred primary region (we'd prefer us-west for proximity to our users).
- Define burst capacity (we expect 3x baseline peaks during evening batch windows).
- Can you share a draft SOW and any pre-provisioning network/KMS requirements we need to prepare?

I'm attaching our initial traffic matrix (regional_capacity_matrix.xlsx) and a short ops note.

Will be on PTO Wed–Thu but monitoring email. Can we target a short sync next week to align owners?

Thanks,
Tom Rivera
Head of ML Ops, AtlasAI
T: +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: regional_capacity_matrix.xlsx (xlsx), ops_notes.txt (txt)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@atlasai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding for AtlasAI

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. We're excited to get AtlasAI live on Dedicated. High-level responses and a proposed mutual action plan below; I'd like to confirm these in a 30-minute sync next Tue (Oct 5).

Primary region recommendation: us-west1 (closest to your traffic and best match for available GPU SKUs). Secondary/fallback: us-central1 for capacity overflow — we will configure routing policies to failover based on latency and instance availability.

Bursting / autoscaling:
- Baseline pool: sized to handle steady QPS you provided in the spreadsheet.
- Burst policy: automatic scale up to 2.5x baseline for sudden spikes, with a pre-warm option to reserve +30% capacity for predictable nightly batch windows (you can request pre-warm windows via the console or API).
- Scaling cooldowns: 5 minute scale-in cooldown, 90s scale-out ramp when concurrent requests exceed threshold.

SOW & runbook: attached is a first-pass SOW (atlas_sow_v2.pdf) and a short SLA/runbook template. Key timeline proposal:
1) Week 0: SOW sign-off + network checklist completed (VPC peering, routes, KMS keys).
2) Week 1: Provision baseline pool in us-west1; internal canary with synthetic traffic.
3) Week 2: Customer canary (10% traffic) -> 50% -> full cutover, with fallback policies tested at each step.

Owners:
- Redwood: Neha (CS lead), Monica (Infra ops), Rishi (SRE / autoscale config)
- AtlasAI: Tom (ML Ops), eng-ops@atlasai.com (network)

I'll add a runbook section that lists exact pre-provision network artifacts needed. Can Monica and Rishi confirm the proposed burst multiplier and cooldowns?

-neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: atlas_sow_v2.pdf (pdf), rdw_sla_runbook_template.md (md)

Quick operational checks from infra:
- Network: we need AtlasAI to confirm the list of CIDR ranges and whether they prefer VPC peering or a VPN tunnel. The attached network_requirements.txt has the checklist (MTU, allowed ports, private IP ranges).
- KMS: will need a cross-account KMS key or an HSM flow — which one do they prefer? If they want Redwood-managed keys, we need explicit approval in the SOW.
- Provisioning lead: Monica -> I'll be the provisioning lead for the pool activation, but I need a named engineering contact from Atlas for switch testing and access.

I agree with the 2.5x burst as a starting point, but we should keep the pre-warm toggle available for predictable batch periods so we don't rely solely on autoscale for big bursts.

Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Infrastructure Program Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: network_requirements.txt (txt)

From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@atlasai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-ops@atlasai.com
Date: 2026-09-30T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding for AtlasAI

Neha / Monica —

Thanks for the proposal. Confirming: primary = us-west1, fallback = us-central1. We prefer VPC peering and will provide CIDRs this week. For KMS, AtlasAI would like customer-managed keys; we'll provide the key ARN and a designated administrator.

Bursting: we can accept the 2.5x baseline as the default, but request a 3x firebreak option for scheduled nightly batches. In those windows we'd like an explicit 30-minute pre-warm reservation to avoid cold-start throttling. Also: can Redwood provide an SLA credit table for missed latency SLA during bursts? We may need that included in the SOW.

I'll loop in our infra lead next week for the Oct 5 sync.

—Tom
Tom Rivera
Head of ML Ops, AtlasAI

Attachment: updated_traffic_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:33:00-07:00
Subject: Plan summary & action owners — AtlasAI Dedicated pool (next steps)

Team —

Summarizing decisions from the thread and setting next actions ahead of the Oct 5 customer sync:
- Regions: primary us-west1, fallback us-central1 (confirmed). Owner: Monica to kick baseline provisioning in us-west1 week of Oct 12.
- Bursting: default 2.5x baseline; customer may request 3x scheduled pre-warm windows (30 min). Owner: Rishi to implement burst policy + pre-warm toggle in staging.
- Security: AtlasAI will provide customer-managed KMS ARN. Monica to validate KMS flow and list any SOW changes.
- Network: Atlas to provide CIDR list and indicate VPC peering preference by Oct 4. Owner: Monica / Marissa to coordinate peering runbook.
- SOW: action to include explicit SLA credit table for burst-period latency failures. Draft updated by Neha and shared to Drive by Oct 2.

Deliverables and timeline:
1) Oct 2 — Updated SOW (Neha) and runbook link posted to Drive.
2) Oct 5 — 30-minute sync (Neha, Monica, Rishi + Atlas infra lead) to confirm canary dates.
3) Week of Oct 12 — Baseline pool provisioning in us-west1 (Monica).

Please comment on any missing items. I'll mark tasks in the deal record and attach the runbook once the SOW is updated.

-neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
